A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IPO research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including all supplementary sections A-E in v3. V1 has no separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original VBench experiments, critic validation accuracies, component ablations, iterative-training results and qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds human preference evaluation, dataset distribution statistics, additional VBench results and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Both retain the VILA critic, iterative generation-labeling-optimization loop, Diffusion-DPO/KTO objectives and real-video regularization. V3 explicitly formulates the critic's existing supervised training loss, but does not establish a new architecture or implemented method component.

E1.justification: Both use CogVideoX-generated preference data, VidGen-1M real videos, VBench evaluation and pairwise/pointwise critic tasks. V3's human evaluation, additional metric breakdowns and examples remain within the existing text-to-video coverage; no distinct new dataset or test scenario is established.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain CogVideoX-2B/5B, DPO versus KTO, and 13B versus 40B critics. Renamed rows and the additional human comparison against CogVideoX-2B do not introduce a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The stated dataset-generation setting changes from three variants per prompt in v1 Section 4.1 to four in v3 Section 3.1; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun. V3 also adds human win/tie comparisons across consistency, motion and faithfulness. The principal training budgets and VBench evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds descriptive analyses of prompt and annotation distributions in Figure 3 and four further qualitative cases in Figure 7. The real-data, critic-scale, DPO/KTO and iteration ablations already existed; the critic analyses are partly relocated to Appendix B.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. V3's human preference percentages provide outcomes without uncertainty reporting. Different random seeds generate video variants in both versions; the changed variant count concerns sampling, not statistical replication.

E6.justification: Headline VBench totals remain 82.74 for IPO and 80.91/81.61 for the 2B/5B baselines. V3 adds human preferences, including 54.6% IPO wins versus 16% baseline wins for motion, and all 16 VBench dimensions. Table 6 revises 40B critic accuracies from 86.14/97.57 to 81.33/85.57 for pairwise/pointwise tasks, although Appendix B.2 inconsistently states 80.73/86.57. V3 also omits four metrics from the no-real-data ablation.

T1.justification: V3 Section 3.3.4 replaces v1's fixed-reward sequence with a recurrence using an iteration-dependent reward r^k and explicitly initializes r^0=0. This is a limited revision of the mathematical account. The KL-regularized alignment and DPO/KTO derivations are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: automatic critic labeling, iterative optimization supporting DPO/KTO, a 2B model surpassing its 5B counterpart, and claimed VBench state of the art. V3's added conclusion restates these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 Appendix E adds substantial qualifications concerning dataset representativeness, critic hallucinations and formatting sensitivity, annotation bias and generalizability, and computational constraints. These limitations were not developed in v1. V3 also expands mechanism interpretations, including claims that iteration mitigates catastrophic forgetting and improves convergence.

D1.justification: V3 Appendix A documents annotator selection, the ten-person annotation team, training, rating criteria, tie rules, quality checks and the interface. Section 3.2 adds explicit critic input and loss details. The abstract changes a future-release promise to reported code/checkpoint availability with a link. Conversely, v1's position-swapping, KTO binary-label mapping and early-stopping details are omitted.

R1.justification: V3 prunes discussion and citations including DDPO, DPOK and Iterative Reasoning Preference Optimization, while retaining the main research context. It newly characterizes prior video post-training approaches as achieving only minor improvements. The central positioning against single-round optimization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V1's separate method and implementation sections are substantially rewritten into dataset, critic-training and alignment subsections. Experimental material is reorganized between the main text and supplement, related work is condensed, and a conclusion is added. The author and affiliation lines also change.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is redrawn, and v3 adds a single-round comparison diagram, distribution plots, human evaluation chart, annotation interface and additional qualitative panels. V1 Figure 2 is retained as v3 Figure 4. Several tables are compacted or relocated; v3 Table 4 introduces metric headers inconsistent with the retained numerical column order.

improvement.justification: V3 improves readability and transparency through clearer organization, detailed annotation guidance, direct human preference evidence and explicit critic/annotation limitations. These gains are limited by unspecified human-study sample sizes and uncertainty, omitted implementation details, and new reporting inconsistencies in Table 4 and Appendix B.2 versus Table 6. The central method and headline benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
